posts.raw_content:
1980:

I needed a part for my toilet, so I purchased one from John, who owns the local hardware store. John then took that money and bought dinner for his family at the restaurant owned by Lillian.

Lillian took that money and got her oil changed at my auto repair shop. I then used that money to buy flowers from Tom, the florist, to give to my wife.

Tom the florist used that money to buy a birthday cake for his daughter at the bakery owned by Betty. Betty used the money she earned at her bakery over the last year to hire Jim, the contractor, to remodel her bathroom. Jim then hired Gery, Michael, and Harry to assist him.

All of the businesses in the community benefited from the financial ecosystem. Payrolls were properly taxed to fund local schools, roads, and government services.

All was well.

2024:

A bunch of local businesses started hiring illegal workers to exploit their cheap labor. They pay the workers under the table, so there is no proper taxation occurring for them to contribute to local schools, government services, etc.

The workers then turn that cash into money orders, which they send electronically back to Mexico to support their families there. Their families then use that money to support their local grocery stores, hardware stores, florists, auto repair shops, etc.

I now need a part for my toilet. The local hardware store is closed because John could not compete with Home Depot, which is where everybody started having to spend their money to get the cheapest price possible in order to compete with businesses using illegal labor.

Because John no longer had a business, he was unable to buy dinner at Lillian’s restaurant, which she had to close anyway because she could not keep her prices competitive with businesses that were using illegal workers.

Because she went out of business, she was unable to pay me to complete the repairs on her vehicle. And because my auto repair business is now in hardship, I am unable to splurge on things like buying flowers from Tom the florist to give to my wife.

Now Tom is having to cut his own expenses, so he is baking a cake for his daughter at home instead of buying one from Betty’s bakery.

Betty had to close her bakery because all of her customers were in the same boat and could not afford discretionary spending on things like cakes. So Betty was unable to hire Jim to complete her bathroom renovation, which meant he could not hire Gery, Michael, or Harry to help him with the job.

So now tons of businesses in the area have gone under. Total revenue is down because those businesses are no longer generating tax revenue.

The illegal workers are facing no hardships because they are still getting paid and still sending money to their families in Mexico. The schools are going to shit because tax revenue is down, crime is going up because the police department is underfunded, and the only businesses opening in the area are mattress stores and Boost Mobile locations.

Illegal. Immigration. Is. Not. A. Victimless. Crime.
